key_insight: Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) recovers correlation lost during stabilizer projection, improving quantum chemistry accuracy while retaining a reduced quantum register.
engineering_relevance: SSPT can reduce the contextual qubits needed for chemically precise energy estimates, making resource-efficient quantum chemistry calculations more practical.
method: Use Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection to generate external states from an optimized reference.
Estimate correlation corrections with Epstein–Nesbet-type second-order perturbation theory or a resolvent retaining external-space couplings.
Evaluate matrix elements through reduced-register Pauli expectation values without reconstructing the full-space wave function.
evidence_signal: Molecular benchmarks show substantially reduced projection-induced energy errors and chemical precision with fewer contextual qubits in several cases, though the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: The measurement and classical processing costs of treating the external manifold require assessment as molecular systems grow.
paper_title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
